# Oxide Launcher 1.3.0

**Oxide Launcher** — an independently maintained Android launcher for Minecraft: Java Edition.

## New visual identity

- A complete design system in `ui/theme/Oxide.kt`: an achromatic palette, the full type ramp, 15px card radii, the surface and rail gradients and every motion constant including the intro timings.
- The Oxide mark is drawn natively as a 45 degree rotated rounded square with a smaller square inset inside it, beside the OX / IDE wordmark.
- The intro now runs over the real interface instead of a separate splash: the UI is composed and rendering from the first frame, an opaque #050505 curtain covers it, and exactly one logo travels from the centre to the measured centre of the sidebar brand slot and stays there. The curtain starts fading at 2450ms of a 3150ms journey, so the interface is already visible while the logo is still in flight. The destination and the landing scale are read from the measured slot, so nothing is hard-coded to one screen size.

## Fast launch: why the previous cache showed no benefit

The preparation cache shipped in 1.2.0 was missing on effectively every launch, and several pieces of repeated work were never cached at all.

- `progressDownloadTasks` schedules the same asset objects twice for any version that still carries `inheritsFrom`. The recorded file count therefore never matched the deduplicated parsed count, so the cache reported itself unreadable on every launch. Counts are now taken after deduplicating by path, and a mismatch is logged with both numbers instead of being misreported.
- The parent version JSON was read from the merged manifest, whose `inheritsFrom` is always null, so it sat outside the fingerprint entirely. It is now read from the raw version JSON.
- `GameManifest.getAssetIndex` synthesises an index with a null sha1 for manifests without an `assetIndex` block, which is the normal case for Fabric, Forge and NeoForge. That made every launch hash the whole index, delete it and re-download it. An index with no declared hash is now reused and only re-downloaded when it fails to parse.
- The merged manifest is cached under the same fingerprint, removing a rebuild and a re-serialise on every launch.
- The APK's `unlist_versions.json` is parsed once per process instead of on every cold start.
- The local file check runs at up to 8-way parallelism instead of a fixed 4, because all that remains is stat calls.

## Measurement

A device test could not previously tell a fast preparation phase from a phase that was never the bottleneck, because the launch path emitted exactly one duration. Added:
- `LAUNCH T0` at the start of the launcher-side launch
- `PREPARE EVAL` and `PREPARE phase` timings
- `GAME PROCESS first frame` in the game process

Together they split a launch into "launcher preparation" and "JVM plus Minecraft", which is what tells you which one to work on next. Expect the preparation phase to be a small fraction of a launch; the rest is Minecraft's own bootstrap.

## CurseForge

The CurseForge integration is configured with an API key through the project's existing `curseforge_api_key` build property. It is only sent as the `x-api-key` request header, never logged and never shown in the interface.

## Branding

The splash notice and the About screen now present the product as Oxide Launcher. The upstream author's avatar, name card and sponsorship link have been replaced with the Oxide project. All legally required attribution is kept: the third-party acknowledgements, the credit for the account code adapted from ZalithLauncher2Plus, and every per-file copyright header.

This build was verified by CI only (compilation, unit tests, lint, R8, packaging, signing) and has not been validated on physical hardware by the project maintainers.

bodies.markdown: New Oxide visual identity with the intro animation over the real UI, and the launch preparation cache fixed so it actually engages.
